[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant offered to recommend easy trails in California.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant asked for clarification on what the user considers "easy" in terms of trail difficulty.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided a list of easy trails in California:  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 1. Runyon Canyon Loop in Los Angeles: A popular, 3.5-mile loop with great views of the Hollywood Hills and the city.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 2. Mirror Lake Trail in Yosemite National Park: A 4-mile out-and-back trail that's relatively flat and takes you to a beautiful lake with reflections of surrounding granite cliffs.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 3. Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve Trails in San Diego: Several short, easy trails with stunning ocean views and unique sandstone formations.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 4. Lands End Trail in San Francisco: A 3.5-mile out-and-back trail along the coastal bluffs with views of the Golden Gate Bridge and the Pacific Ocean.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 5. Echo Mountain Trail in the San Gabriel Mountains: A 6.5-mile out-and-back trail with minimal elevation gain and great views of the surrounding mountains.  
[EVENT] User expressed interest in the Mirror Lake Trail in Yosemite.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant confirmed that the Mirror Lake Trail is a wonderful choice for a beginner-friendly hike.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided tips and details about the Mirror Lake Trail:  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 1. The trail is a 4-mile out-and-back with minimal elevation gain (about 100 feet).  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 2. The trail is paved for the first mile, then turns into a dirt path.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 3. Parking is limited near the trailhead; consider using the free shuttle bus from the Yosemite Valley Visitor Center.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 4. Best time to visit is early morning or late afternoon for better reflections.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 5. Bring plenty of water and snacks, as there are no services along the trail.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 6. No permit is needed for this trail, but parking and entrance fees apply.
